title: Utility Account Standing in Home-Site Lease Nonpayment Cure Periods
content:
**Collections standard — utility standing extension**

The cure period of a nonpayment notice on a Home-Site Lease is lengthened by a utility-standing extension, in days, read from the Utility Pass-Through Service statement account serving the site.

| Utility late fee on the Utility Pass-Through Service account in the trailing twelve calendar months | Utility balance | Utility-standing extension |
|---|---|---|
| none | zero or a credit | 2 days |
| none | an amount owing | 1 day |
| one or more | any | none |

**Notes**

1. The account read is the utility statement account serving the leased site, not the rent ledger of the Home-Site Lease.
2. A utility balance of exactly zero falls on the 2-day row with a credit balance.
3. A utility late fee posted more than twelve calendar months before the notice is outside the window.

*Hypothetical.* A utility account with no late fee in the past year and a balance of 0.00: 2 days. The same account with 64.80 owing: 1 day. An account with a utility late fee posted five months ago: none, whatever its balance.
